 Last Update October 18, 2026, 10:08 PM EDT 16 days until midterms, Trump rallies GOP as Johnson predicts Republicans will hold House
 President Donald Trump is intensifying his campaign push for Republican candidates as Democrats target the president and House Speaker Mike Johnson works to defend the GOP’s narrow majority.
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Flipboard 
 Share by Email 
 WHAT TO KNOW
 President Donald Trump rallied Republicans in Kentucky over the weekend, tying the party’s midterm prospects to his second-term agenda and warning that Democrats could reverse his policies.
 House Speaker Mike Johnson says Republicans will retain control of the chamber despite voter frustration over high prices, the war with Iran and the GOP’s narrow margin.
 Democrats are intensifying attacks on Trump while focusing on competitive Senate races in Georgia, Michigan and Texas and working to regain control of Congress.
 25 Posts Sort by Newest Oldest incoming update… Coverage for this event has ended.
 6 hours ago Pinned Former Biden pollster warns Democrats falling short on youth turnout 
 Kellyanne Conway warned Sunday that Democratic enthusiasm in polls may not translate into votes, while former Biden campaign pollster Celinda Lake said her party has fallen short on investing in youth turnout.
 “Participation in a poll is not the same as participation at the polls,” Conway said on “Fox News Sunday.”
 The Fox News contributor argued some Republicans are reluctant to answer surveys and said competitive Senate races remain “on a razor’s edge.”
 Lake countered that Democrats lead on enthusiasm but urged voters against letting favorable polling keep them home.
 “It’s important for people at this point in time not to listen to the polls,” she said. “And when a pollster tells you that, you know you should believe it.”
 Lake also credited Republicans and Turning Point USA with doing a better job investing in youth turnout.
 “I do think that we have had insufficient investment, particularly in youth turnout,” she said.
 Conway also questioned election prediction markets, arguing they cannot reliably determine who will actually vote.
 “The threshold question is whether to bother at all,” she said.
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 5 hours ago Bernie Sanders brands Trump ‘most dangerous president’ at Florida midterm event 
 Sen. Bernie Sanders branded President Donald Trump “the most dangerous president” in U.S. history during an event with Angie Nixon in Tallahassee, Florida.
 The Vermont independent accused Trump of being an “authoritarian type” who “does not believe in democracy,” pointing to freedoms of dissent and the press that Americans have fought to protect.
 He also called Trump “a narcissist” and “a pathological liar,” telling his “conservative friends” that people try to raise their children to be honest.
 “We can disagree with each other. That’s called democracy,” Sanders said. “But we don’t have to lie every day.”
 Sanders also accused Trump of insulting people over their backgrounds or countries of origin.
 “That is not what a president is supposed to do,” he said.
 Sanders added, “This is the most important midterm election in modern American history, period. End of discussion.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 6 hours ago Gingrich urges Americans to reject ‘gloom and doom’ and embrace a ‘golden age’ 
 Former House Speaker Newt Gingrich urged Americans to look beyond political infighting Sunday, arguing technological breakthroughs could unlock decades of opportunity.
 “Let’s get past this gloom and doom. Let’s get past all this bickering and infighting,” Gingrich said on “Life, Liberty & Levin.”
 Discussing his new book, “America’s Golden Age: Trumpism and an Era of Limitless Possibilities,” Gingrich said advances in artificial intelligence , robotics, medicine and space exploration could transform Americans’ lives.
 He argued the biggest changes will come as those technologies work together, expanding what people can accomplish physically and intellectually.
 Gingrich also predicted medical advances could shift health care toward preventing illness rather than treating people after they become sick.
 “The current system is totally obsolete,” he said. “There’s no reason for it to be this expensive.”
 Gingrich cast his book as a push to restore confidence in America’s future as the country marks its 250th anniversary.
 “The number one purpose of this book is to reignite optimism,” he said. “We’re headed towards an exciting future, a dynamic future.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 6 hours ago AOC draws criticism for saying ‘working class’ was code for race and gender 
 Fox News contributor Tomi Lahren criticized Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez over her comments about working-class political messaging and her response to questions about Democratic Socialists of America policies.
 “For a very long time, working class was a euphemism for race and gender,” Ocasio-Cortez said in an MS NOW interview. “It was really about a very specific and only one slice of the working class.”
 Lahren contrasted those remarks with President Donald Trump’s economic pitch, arguing he focuses on working Americans “regardless of race or gender.”
 Lahren also accused the New York Democrat of distancing herself from the DSA when questioned about its platform.
 In the clip, Ocasio-Cortez argued candidates should be judged on their own proposals.
 “We need to be operating with what these candidates ran on,” she said, rather than what “some organization somewhere in our country is saying.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 7 hours ago Democrats blasted for treating Trump administration jobs like a ‘scarlet letter’ 
 Fox News contributor Tomi Lahren accused Democrats of trying to shame young conservatives out of working for the Trump administration, blasting Sen. Elissa Slotkin as disconnected from young voters. 
 “Have they learned nothing?” Lahren said while reacting to remarks she characterized as discouraging young Americans from taking administration jobs.
 Democrats treating those jobs as “a scarlet letter” is “utterly ridiculous,” she said, calling the approach “tone deaf and removed … from the real world.”
 Lahren pointed to young men who supported President Donald Trump in 2024, while acknowledging Republicans still have work to do with younger voters.
 “We’ve got to win young women. We’ve gotta win back young men in a lot of ways, and the economy and the war have a lot to do with that,” she said.
 Lahren also rejected the Michigan senator’s reputation as a moderate.
 “People would look at Slotkin and say that this is a moderate Democrat,” she said. “This is not a moderate Democrat.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 8 hours ago Donalds dismisses Clinton’s potential Florida impact, touts Trump, DeSantis backing 
 Rep. Byron Donalds brushed off Bill Clinton’s potential impact on Florida’s elections Sunday, arguing the Democratic Party has moved beyond the former president.
 “This isn’t Bill Clinton’s Democrat Party anymore. This isn’t JFK’s Democrat Party anymore,” Donalds told “The Sunday Briefing.” “This is now the Democrat Party of Bernie Sanders and AOC.”
 The Republican gubernatorial candidate was responding to a question about Florida Democrats seeking Clinton’s help on the campaign trail.
 “I don’t think it’s going to have much of an impact overall,” Donalds said.
 Donalds also touted endorsements from President Donald Trump and Gov. Ron DeSantis, pledging to continue Florida’s conservative policies on taxes, public safety and parental rights.
 “The same standards and principles that have made us the envy of the other 49 states will continue going forward,” he said.
 Asked about unrest in France, Donalds argued leaders must draw a firm line between peaceful protests and violence.
 “If you’re going to riot and loot, that just was never going to be tolerated,” he said of Florida’s approach.
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 9 hours ago Newsom warns 2028 may lack ‘free and fair election’ unless Democrats win midterms 
 California Gov. Gavin Newsom warned Democrats that a “free and fair election” in 2028 could hinge on their winning key congressional races this year.
 “It is all on the line in 2026,” Newsom said in a video shared on X. “Do not focus on 2028.”
 “We may not have a free and fair election in 2028 unless Maggie is back in the majority and Chris is in the United States Senate,” he added, referring to New Hampshire Democratic Reps. Maggie Goodlander and Chris Pappas.
 Newsom offered no evidence in the clip to support that warning.
 “It’s a fact, not hyperbole,” he said.
 In the accompanying post, Newsom urged voters to send Pappas to the Senate and help Goodlander reclaim a Democratic House majority.
 “The stakes couldn’t be higher,” he wrote. “Get out and VOTE.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 11 hours ago Former NFL kicker makes final push to keep key Arizona seat in GOP hands 
 Republican Jay Feely rejected his Democratic opponent’s “rubber stamp” attack Sunday as the former NFL kicker fights for a competitive Arizona House seat. 
 “Well, I think I’m a rubber stamp for the first congressional district of Arizona,” Feely told “The Sunday Briefing.”
 Feely faces Democrat Amish Shah in a race Fox News Power Rankings rates “lean Democrat.”
 Asked about an Axios report that former independent Sen. Kyrsten Sinema voted for him in the Republican primary, Feely welcomed her support and stressed his willingness to engage voters who disagree with him.
 Feely said the economy and border security remain top voter concerns. He also defended data centers, provided communities have a say and residents are protected from higher electricity costs.
 “When you have those parameters, then they’re a win for the local economy,” he said.
 Feely said his campaign has knocked on more than 500,000 doors, including homes displaying Shah’s signs.
 “I’m willing to listen to you, to hear you, to respect you, and then to go and represent you in DC.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 12 hours ago Former Trump Treasury official warns Fed rate hike would be a ‘mistake’ 
 Former Deputy Treasury Secretary Michael Faulkender warned Sunday that another interest rate hike could squeeze the economy without fixing the oil supply pressures he blamed for rising prices.
 “I do think they’re ultimately gonna raise rates, but I think it’s a mistake,” Faulkender said on “Sunday Morning Futures,” ahead of the Federal Reserve’s Oct. 28 decision.
 “They have no control over oil supply.”
 Faulkender argued higher borrowing costs would depress other parts of the economy while doing little to curb fuel demand from truckers or slow the construction of artificial intelligence data centers. 
 He said easing tensions in the Middle East and productivity gains from AI could help cool inflation, warning a rate hike could hit after those benefits begin taking hold.
 Faulkender instead urged the Fed to focus on shrinking its balance sheet, arguing that would better anchor inflation expectations than a quarter-point rate increase.
 He also took aim at government expansion and tax increases, arguing they would shift resources away from businesses.
 “They call it Medicare for all, I call it the DMV for all,” Faulkender said. “That is neither an improvement for the American people nor something that is going to take inflationary pressure off.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 13 hours ago Whatley vows to beat Cooper in North Carolina Senate showdown, pushes back on ad spending questions 
 Republican Michael Whatley predicted victory in North Carolina’s Senate showdown Sunday, dismissing a Democratic edge and pushing back on questions about his campaign’s ad spending.
 “Well, we’re going to win this race,” Whatley told “The Sunday Briefing” when asked about Fox News Power Rankings rating the race “likely Democrat.”
 The former RNC chairman faces former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper for retiring Republican Sen. Thom Tillis’ seat.
 Asked about a Politico report that his campaign had no future traditional TV ad reservations booked, Whatley said spending had shifted toward digital and streaming.
 “Well, we’re not dark. We are reaching voters all day, every day,” he said.
 Whatley said he has visited all 100 counties and held more than 400 campaign events. He argued turnout will decide the contest in a state President Donald Trump carried three straight times.
 On affordability, Whatley blamed Cooper and former President Joe Biden for rising costs.
 “What we need to do is have people make more and keep more,” he said.
 Whatley also cast Cooper as a vote for Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer’s agenda.
 “The first vote I’m going to cast is going to be for North Carolina.”
 Posted by Stepheny Price Share 14 hours ago Ilhan Omar should be jailed, deported if citizenship fraud proven, Top House Republican says 
 EXCLUSIVE: The highest-ranking House lawmaker from Rep. Ilhan Omar's home state is calling for the embattled progressive to be jailed and deported if it is found that she or her father lied on federal paperwork to get her U.S. citizenship.
 Omar, D-Minn., is under federal investigation over allegations she or her father lied about her birth year on immigration paperwork to obtain her citizenship when her family fled Somalia in the late 1990s. She and other Democrats, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., have denounced the probe as political persecution of one of President Donald Trump's detractors weeks before a critical election.
 But Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., the No. 3 leader in the House of Representatives, told Fox News Digital "there have been rumors for years" about Omar and, if proven true, she should face consequences.
 "I would say, first, she should probably serve time in the gray bar motel and then get the hell out of here. She should go back to where she came from" if the allegations are proven to be true, Emmer said. "If it's determined that she lied to gain citizenship, then, absolutely, she should go back to the front of the line."
 Omar is a member of the House "Squad," a far-left clique that includes Reps. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.
 Federal agents raided Omar's Washington, D.C., home earlier this week and took her cellphone and other possessions.
 The allegations stem from her father becoming a U.S. citizen in 2000. Omar was believed to be 17 at the time, and, as a minor, automatically qualified for citizenship under U.S. law along with him.
 But, recently, it’s been alleged she was actually 18 and would have needed to go through the process herself at that point.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Elizabeth Elkind. 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 14 hours ago Bernie Sanders admits Democrats failed working-class voters on economics, driving them to Trump 
 Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., acknowledged on Saturday that Democrats failed working-class Americans economically, contributing to voters abandoning the party for President Donald Trump.
 When asked during an interview on MS NOW what exactly Democrats had done wrong to lose working-class voters to Trump, Sanders pointed to the party's economic record, arguing that its failure to address their financial struggles had contributed to declining support.
 "What I think what Trump did, again — this gets back to my view — that the Democratic Party failed working-class people on economic issues," Sanders said.
  "I think they have a lot to be proud of in terms of fighting for civil rights, for women's rights, for gay rights, for environmental stuff, but in terms of working-class issues, no, I don't think they've done a good job," he added.
 Sanders, an independent, pointed to unfulfilled economic promises and trade agreements he blamed for the loss of American manufacturing jobs as reasons working-class voters became disillusioned with the party.
 "What they did is for years, they heard the Democrats say, 'Oh, we're going to do this, we're going to do that, and we're going to help you.' And they didn't. And it's true. Democrats pushed through terrible trade deals, which cost us millions of good-paying manufacturing jobs, et cetera, et cetera. They lost faith in the Democratic Party, and not unjustifiably. All right?" Sanders said.
 When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, Republican National Committee national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre criticized Democrats' economic policies and argued that the party had abandoned working families.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' CJ Womak. 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 15 hours ago Obama accuses Trump administration of targeting Ilhan Omar for deportation over political criticism 
 Former President Barack Obama accused the Trump administration of weaponizing the federal government against its political enemies in a social media post defending Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., amid an investigation into the progressive lawmaker's citizenship.
 Obama claimed the administration is attempting to strip Omar of her U.S. citizenship and deport her over her criticism of President Donald Trump, warning that the effort could set a dangerous precedent.
 "It is a basic principle of American democracy that the government can’t selectively target individuals simply because of their political beliefs or what they say," Obama wrote Sunday on X. "But that’s exactly what the Trump Administration is doing to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota."
 Obama's remarks come after federal agents searched Omar's Washington, D.C., home as part of a criminal investigation into her immigration status.
 Sources previously told Fox News Digital that investigators are examining whether Omar or her father committed fraud on immigration paperwork when she became a U.S. citizen decades ago.
 Obama defended the circumstances under which Omar became a U.S. citizen, saying, "To understand why this is so appalling, it’s important to know the facts."
 Obama then said Omar arrived in the United States with her father at age 12 and automatically became a citizen at 17 when her father was naturalized.
 The former president accused investigators of pursuing an "unsubstantiated theory" that Omar was actually 18 at the time, which he said would have required her to apply for citizenship separately.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Stephen Sorace. 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 15 hours ago Bernie Sanders claims Elon Musk, billionaires are 'afraid' of Angie Nixon 
 Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt, threw his weight behind Angie Nixon's campaign in Florida on Sunday, bashing billionaires and Elon Musk at a campaign rally.
 Sanders told the crowd that Republicans have the "money," but "we have the people."
 "We are dealing with a corrupt campaign finance system. Today, and it's important for everybody to think about this. Why is Elon Musk spending over $300 million in Florida and all over this country to make sure they're trying to make sure that Republicans retain control over the House and the Senate? Why are other billionaires flooding the airwaves with dishonest ads? And what that is about is they are afraid," Sanders said.
 Sanders went on to call out President Donald Trump for reneging on his promise to end America's wars abroad.
 "We have got to end endless wars. Wars that are illegal, wars that are unconstitutional. All of you know what the president of the United States does not, and that the authority for going to war in the Constitution rests with Congress. And when Angie gets to Washington, she and I will work with others to make sure that we end this war in Iran and that we stop providing billions and billions of dollars to the extremist government in Israel, who have been doing terrible things to the Palestinian people," Sanders said to a cheering crowd.
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 16 hours ago Meet the 22-year-old candidate eyeing history in key swing state as Gen Z embraces conservatism 
 From delivering pizzas to running for an Iowa House seat, 22-year-old Dillon Fillion hopes to make history in his swing district and inspire Gen Z to embrace conservatism, which he says he's already seeing on the ground.
 Fillion, believed to be the youngest candidate ever to seek office in Scott County, spoke to Fox News Digital about his ambitions to cut property taxes, boost police funding, give parents more say in their children’s education and draw Gen Z to the polls.
 "I think people are very excited that a young person is running because they see a lot of these old people running for office. No offense to them, but people wanna see some fresh new faces, and I think it's time for my generation to step up," Fillion said.
 Before launching his bid for the Iowa House, Fillion decided to take a gap year from Scott Community College, where he is pursuing a criminal justice degree. He works as a Domino’s delivery driver while hitting the campaign trail, which he described as juggling "two full-time jobs."
 "Basically, I do a full-time job as well as campaigning," he said.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Kiera McDonald. 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 17 hours ago 'No Kings' foot soldiers ignore organizers' warning, go all in for Democrats 
 WASHINGTON, D.C. — As the high-level organizers of the "No Kings" demonstrations seek to turn their operation into a nationwide get-out-the-vote rally Saturday, their warning to steer clear of partisan messaging that could violate their own rules is falling on deaf ears.
 A Fox News Digital investigation reveals that, on the ground, the political activation is, in fact, highly partisan, led by the center-left Indivisible nonprofit that has received millions of dollars of funding from Democratic megadonor George Soros. "No Kings" organizers didn't respond to a request for comment.
 The partisan nature of the day's events is important because political experts say the "No Kings" operation reveals a sophisticated electoral strategy: transform the crowds assembled for anti-Trump protests into a durable voter bloc that participates in elections and turns out a "Blue Tsunami" of votes in political battles. But federal election law bars nonprofits, many of which fund the "No Kings" operation, from advocating for particular candidates.
 Behind today's action, Fox News Digital has identified a sprawling network of 300 progressive advocacy organizations, labor unions, Democratic political operatives and tax-exempt nonprofits with an estimated $2.5 billion in annual revenues, transforming the "No Kings" protest movement into a nationwide voter-mobilization operation of an estimated 3,000 events for Democrats.
 A review of digital advertisements for Saturday's "No Kings: Vote Early" demonstrations and their organizing rhetoric identifies multiple instances of organizers promoting the very language the coalition's national rulebook forbids in its attempt to create the illusion of nonpartisanship.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Asra Nomani. 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 17 hours ago Who will control the Senate after the midterm elections? Nine key races could decide 
 Democrats have expanded their once-narrow path to reclaiming the Senate majority with just over two weeks until Election Day, but they'll need to win several competitive races to take control of the chamber.
 If Democrats ride a massive blue wave in the midterm elections, they could end up with 52 or even 53 seats in the next Senate. But if Republicans out-perform the polls, they could hold their majority, which currently stands at 53-47.
 Here's a look at the current battlefield and both parties' routes to securing a Senate majority in the midterms.
 The latest Power Rankings point to Democrats and Republicans each taking 47 seats in the midterms, leaving six races rated as true toss-ups. Additionally, three races are rated as leaners — one step shy of a toss-up. These nine showdowns will likely determine whether the Democrats make a net gain of four seats to win control of the Senate or if the GOP holds the majority.
 "Nine races will determine control of the Senate, and on the polling alone, you could call any of them toss-ups," said Remy Numa, a Fox News contributor who steers the network's Power Rankings.
 The GOP is fighting political history, as the party in power in Washington has traditionally lost seats during midterm election years. Republicans also face a challenging political climate fueled by persistent inflation Americans see at the grocery store, high gas prices tied to what polls show is an unpopular war with Iran and President Donald Trump's increasingly negative approval ratings.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Paul Steinhauser 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 18 hours ago Minnesota Senate race takes bizarre turn after dark family history uncovered 
 A dark chapter in the family history of Minnesota Democratic Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan has made its way into the race, but it is unclear whether voters will hold the alleged sins of her long-dead grandfather against her. 
 Earlier this week, Alpha News revealed the troubled mental health history of Flanagan's grandfather, John Jacob Hartmann, supported by old newspaper accounts and court records. He spent decades in psychiatric custody, escaped twice and was suspected in multiple killings, though never charged.
 The reporting comes just weeks before the midterm elections, in which Flanagan, the state's lieutenant governor, faces former television sports reporter Michelle Tafoya in a race to fill the seat of Democrat Tina Smith, who is retiring.
 Neither Flanagan nor Tafoya has commented publicly on the matter since the decades-old allegations resurfaced. But the bizarre development has generated a buzz on social media.
 Turning Point USA spokesman Andrew Kolvet highlighted the "violent mental illness in Minnesota Democrat Peggy Flanagan's family," in an X post, followed by a photo of Flanagan wearing a shirt that says "Protect trans kids." and Dustin Grage, a columnist with Town Hall, wrote the report "adds up."
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Elaine Mallon. 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 19 hours ago Michigan Democrat confirms sister-in-law's terror watchlist lawsuit days before Obama campaign stop 
 Michigan Democrat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed acknowledged Saturday night that his sister-in-law was involved in a federal terrorist watchlist lawsuit during the Obama administration, just days before former President Barack Obama is scheduled to campaign alongside him.
 El-Sayed was confronted by Fox News senior correspondent Mike Tobin about court documents identifying his sister-in-law, Mariam Jukaku, as a plaintiff in a 2016 lawsuit challenging her alleged placement on the federal Terrorism Screening Database, commonly known as the terrorist watchlist.
 "There's reporting in a lawsuit that now backs it up. And documentation with the lawsuit that Mariam Jukaku, who's your sister-in-law, that she was on the terrorist watch list?" Tobin asked.
 "Yeah," El-Sayed responded.
 El-Sayed then defended his sister-in-law, insisting she had committed no wrongdoing and turning his criticism toward Republican Senate rival Mike Rogers.
 "She did nothing wrong and was captured on that and then sued and got off," El-Sayed said. "You've got this system where folks are guilty until proven innocent because they've got different kinds of names, because of the infrastructure that people like Mike Rogers set up."
 The exchange comes as Obama prepares to campaign alongside El-Sayed in Michigan on Oct. 24, ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm election.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News Jasmine Baehr. 
 Posted by Anders Hagstrom Share 20 hours ago Top takeaways from JD Vance town hall: Why gas costs too much, DC corruption, immigration hot takes 
 Vice President JD Vance faced questions from Michigan voters during a town hall in Flat Rock as the state emerges as a key battleground in the fight for Senate control in November's midterms.
 The town hall hosted by CBS News came just weeks before the midterm elections as Republicans are fighting to keep their majorities in the House and Senate. Vying for the open Senate seat in Michigan is Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Republican candidate Mike Rogers, a former member of the House of Representatives.
 Here are the top moments from the town hall:
 Vance places blame on Biden administration for high gas prices 
 The first question Vance fielded Saturday came from a 43-year-old Detroit barber, who asked him why gas prices remain significantly higher than during Trump's first term.
 Vance first pointed to Iran’s attacks on commercial shipping and the resulting disruption to global energy markets, but he also placed blame on the Biden administration.
 "That's actually the biggest reason why gas prices are so high, because when Joe Biden was president, we had about 20% of American refining capacity that went offline," Vance said.
 Vance said the Trump administration was using the Defense Production Act to help restore domestic refining capacity, but cautioned that rebuilding that infrastructure would take time.
 CBS News anchor Tony Dokoupil pushed back on Vance's attempts to blame Biden, noting that Trump and Vance have been in office for nearly two years while Americans continued to face high gas prices.
 Vance pressed on White House corruption allegations 
 Dokoupil shifted the conversation to government corruption, citing a Fox News poll showing that 60% of voters were extremely concerned about the issue. He asked Vance whether anything he had witnessed inside the Trump White House made him feel "squeamish."
 "You certainly see evidence of corruption in Washington, D.C. Do I see evidence of corruption from the president of the United States, from the administration? No, Tony, I just don’t," Vance said.
 The exchange came days after Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned as U.S. ambassador to Greece amid allegations that she sought $100,000 from a donor seeking access to Trump administration officials. Guilfoyle has denied wrongdoing.
 Dokoupil pressed Vance on the allegations involving Guilfoyle, along with concerns about restrictions on IRS scrutiny of Trump's tax returns and the president's cryptocurrency earnings.
 This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Elaine Mallon.
